TOP: SignDrop Windows zero-day hands users System rights
AntiFox pentest tool tied to AWS secrets theft; Apache mod_http2 RCE
Project Zero moves to fixed 'Full X' disclosure
Microsoft 365 outage ends; kagent 1.0 brings agents to Kubernetes

P.h: SignDrop Windows zero-day gives a standard user System rights
P.p: TLDR InfoSec reports that researcher Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a Windows zero-day abusing the Common Log File System, Windows Defender, symbolic links and file permissions. Defender opens a user-created CLFS container, then CLFS creates a missing authentication file with Defender's System privileges.
P.s: The researcher says it can bypass antivirus tamper protection. It reportedly works on Windows 11 26H2 and Windows Server 2025 Experimental when CLFS authentication mode is 0 or 1. No patch is mentioned yet.

items.h: AntiFox AI pentest tool linked to AWS secrets theft
items.d: Arctic Wolf ties the open-source platform to intrusions via IIS web shells. Attackers pulled AWS credentials and reached production Secrets Manager and S3. AWS says its services were not compromised. Use least privilege, IMDSv2, GuardDuty.

items.h: Apache mod_http2 heap flaw allows unauthenticated RCE
items.d: TLDR DevOps: fixed in HTTP Server 2.4.71 on Nov 11. Affects 2.4.55 to 2.4.70, scored 9.8 by Red Hat. A public proof of concept shows heap corruption; no RCE exploit released.

items.h: Uber drivers' licenses stolen via Fireworks AI breach
items.d: Attackers stole Fireworks credentials, then accessed Uber data. Uber is notifying thousands of drivers.

items.h: TSMC employee data leaked through a cloud provider
items.d: A threat actor auctioned 6.9GB. TSMC says its own systems were not breached. Claimed data includes national IDs, addresses and banking details.

items.h: Project Zero drops 90+30 for fixed 'Full X' disclosure
items.d: Bugs go public a fixed number of days after report, patched or not. Window: 90 days, 60 from Feb 2, 2027, 30 from Jan 3, 2028. Reason: LLMs make exploits from patches nearly instant.

items.h: Shopify's Cyber Chaos Monkey attacks its own production
items.d: Agentic hunter with test credentials found dozens of serious issues in tens of thousands of runs. A separate judge agent on a different model ends rule-breaking runs.

items.h: OpenAI ships Daybreak Defense Factory and Codex Security
items.d: Findings become engineer-ready patches. The Codex Security CLI scans repos, verifies fixes and exports SARIF, with GitHub Action cost limits.

items.h: 1Password for Agents hides passwords from AI agents
items.d: The agent logs in after user approval; the extension fills credentials only on the matching page.

P.h: Microsoft restores services after multi-day global outage
P.p: TLDR IT says Microsoft restored service to all customers after an outage hit Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot and connected services from Thursday into Saturday. Servers failing automated health checks contributed, and first recovery attempts did not give the expected relief.
P.s: Separately, Microsoft will raise commercial cloud prices 15.7% in India and 10% in New Zealand from January 1, 2027, while cutting them in China, Australia and Norway.

tiles.t: Claude Meetings joins Google Meet calls
tiles.d: Beta for Team and Enterprise. Answers questions, drafts docs, captures actions. Granola, Gong, Fireflies, Otter integrations planned.

tiles.t: AWS Secrets Manager replicates across accounts
tiles.d: Synced secrets without shared KMS keys.
Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google and Meta back the open inference engine.
Event inbox, durable timers, persistent memory, permission system and outbound outbox. TLDR and TLDR IT both flag the post.

P.h: kagent 1.0 GA runs AI agents as actors on Kubernetes
P.p: TLDR DevOps reports kagent 1.0, an enterprise distribution of Agent Substrate. It fixes pod-per-agent limits by scheduling agents as actors on warm worker pools, suspending idle actors to free compute and restoring them when requests arrive.
P.s: Agent Substrate is now a CNCF project. Related: Google Cloud made its Organization Policy MCP server generally available, with Gemini-written custom constraints.

tiles.d: Beta spending limits that pause Workers and Durable Objects at a threshold, with near real-time cost monitoring.
Hosts keep 100 to 200 records, learned lazily over VXLAN.
KV transfer latency for Qwen3 235B falls to about 230 ms.
Kueue and the Coscheduling plugin place pods together on hardware with the right GPU bandwidth.
Skyscanner and incident.io pick it first.

items.h: Petition to reinstate Jensen Huang at Nvidia passes 160,000
items.d: Reportedly backed by Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney and Garry Tan. Huang is under investigation, which will likely block a return.

items.h: Apple bets Siri AI apps will sell its 2027 smart glasses
items.d: The developer ecosystem is the differentiator against Meta and Google.

items.h: SpaceX catches Starship with the tower arms
items.d: Both launch system sections have now been caught on different missions.

items.h: Italy fines Meta $887M over Android photo access
items.d: Gallery suggestions used one app-wide consent. About 20 million Italian users affected.
